Team / Liam —

Attaching a short playbook and a sample metrics file. High-level recommendations (engineer-focused, TL;DR first):

1) Quantization roadmap
  - Start pilot with INT8 variants for the primary workload. Why: predictable accuracy drop <1% on our evals for finance prompts, and kernel support across our fleet.
  - If you need further cost reduction, trial our 4-bit per-layer mixed scheme (we call it q4f): expect incremental savings beyond INT8 but run regression tests on VAT-like table outputs.

2) Batching and batching window tuning
  - For a 300 req/min peak with avg latency target ~250ms P95, use adaptive batching with max_batch_size=32 and a dynamic window cap at 30ms. That yields good throughput while keeping tail latency bounded.
  - Continuous batching (our runtime) will coalesce concurrent in-flight requests; set request_priority for critical routes so they bypass long batch windows.

3) KV/prefix caching strategy
  - Enable prefix KV cache for multi-turn flows where first-party prefixes are reused; this can reduce model compute by ~12-18% in steady-state for short dialogs.
  - Use a 10-minute TTL for session-level caches; tune by cache hit-rate (aim >= 60% for best economics).

4) Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs
  - Hosted + smart routing: projected ~25-35% unit savings combining INT8 + caching + credits in pilot. Works well for variable traffic up to a few hundred rps.
  - Dedicated: recommended if you require consistent P99 latency <350ms at sustained >500 rps or want isolation for regulatory reasons. Dedicated also allows custom kernel pins (slight extra savings).

5) Measurement & evals
  - We'll produce a baseline run (unquantized) and an INT8 run; compare token-level latency, token-loss/ROUGE-like metrics for text quality, and a small sample of finance outputs for spot checks.

See attached: optimizer_quant_playbook.pdf (short technical playbook) and pilot-metrics-sample.csv (simulated deltas).
